html:
The Ljubljana Marshes Wheel is a wooden wheel with its axle, about 5,100 to 5,350 years old, found in 2002 in the marshes south of Ljubljana in Slovenia. It is the oldest wooden wheel yet discovered.

It was made of ash planks, with an oak axle that turned together with the wheel. People of the Copper Age lived here in pile dwellings on the shores of a lake. The find shows that the wheel was in use in Central Europe about as early as in Mesopotamia. The pile dwellings of the Ljubljana Marshes are part of the World Heritage listing of prehistoric pile dwellings around the Alps. The wheel is shown in the city museum of Ljubljana.
